% RETURN, REBASED · EOD 2026-08-21
CYCLICALS LEADCyclicals +2.2% vs defensives on the month
Rotation ReadCitrini · claude

The rotation is cyclical, but it's not an everything melt up. Energy leads all sectors by a wide margin with XLE up 8.97% on the month and a year to date return of 39.65%. Health care is the other powerhouse, XLV up 7.58% one month, but the real thrust is down the market cap scale and into real assets. Gold miners top the theme board, averaging 34.9% monthly gains, a number that dwarfs anything tech or growth is producing. Software and SaaS baskets are recovering sharply, with Software up 15.7% and SaaS up 17.9%, but these are bottom bounce moves after a brutal stretch, not leadership. The Mag 7 basket is flat on the month at -0.1% with a year to date of just 2.4%, and banks are down -2.6%. The signal is clear: you're seeing a rotation out of rate sensitive mega cap duration and into commodity producers, miners, and the life sciences complex, with a side bet on mean reversion in beaten down software names.

The central tension is a risk on rotation that is outright hostile to the long duration assets that have led the prior cycle. The most stretched ratio on the board is GDX over GLD at a z-score of 2.57, sitting in the top fraction of its one year range. This is supported by XLE over XLU at 2.28, also in the top of its range. On the surface, that's a classic reflation trade. But look deeper: every cross-asset ratio involving Treasuries is screaming stress in bonds. HYG over TLT, JNK over TLT, AGG over TLT, MBB over TLT, and EMB over TLT all have z-scores above 2.00 and sit in the top 2% to 3% of their yearly ranges. This isn't just equities outperforming bonds; credit and even agency MBS are massively outperforming long duration government debt. The market is not pricing a recession, it is pricing a sustained high rate regime where you want credit risk and inflation protection, and you want nothing to do with the long end of the Treasury curve. The short end of the curve is getting crushed relative to the long end as well, with SHY over TLT at 2.25. The TLT over IEF ratio is at -2.11, in the bottom 4% of its range. You are being told to avoid duration at all costs and to own things that work when nominal growth is strong and the Fed is not your friend.

What pulls this together is the IBB over XLV ratio, also stretched at a z-score of 2.08 and in the top of its one year range. Combined with the XLV sector performance, you're getting a clean read: the market is bidding biotech and pharma as a growth defensives group that also benefits from the same rate sensitivity dynamic hurting tech. The rotation is broadening into healthcare along with energy and materials. The trade is to stay long the commodity reflation leg through gold miners and energy, with a secondary pulse in healthcare, and to use any short term pop in the Mag 7 or long duration Treasuries as a sell. The one data point that would flip this read is a collapse in the GDX/GLD ratio below a z-score of 1.5, which would signal the gold equity premium is eroding and the reflation trade is cracking.

Relentless rotation into real assets and credit risk, outright rejection of long duration bonds.

BULL

Commodity producers, gold miners, and energy lead with historic momentum, while credit spreads remain tight, signaling a durable risk-on environment driven by nominal growth.

BEAR

Every stretched ratio involves bonds underperforming equities, credit, and hard assets, which is a bet on sticky inflation and a hawkish Fed that will eventually break risk appetite.

TELL

The GDX/GLD ratio breaking below a z-score of 1.5 would indicate the gold equity premium is fading and the cyclical bid is exhausted.

⚠ Cyclical sectors XLE and XLB lead, with defensive XLU lagging badly, a clear reflation rotation. vs Defensive XLV is the second strongest sector, up **7.58%** monthly, while high beta themes like Fintech and Semis are flat to down.: Healthcare is absorbing flows as a duration sensitive defensive that also benefits from the same rate dynamic hurting tech, making this a bifurcated rotation rather than a pure cyclical surge. Trust the reflation read because it is confirmed by commodity ratios and credit performance.

Every ratio touching a z-score of 2.00 or higher is a bet against long duration Treasuries. GDX/GLD at 2.57, HYG/LQD at 2.53, and XLE/XLU at 2.28 are pure trend extensions that you do not fade without a catalyst.

The entire Credit / Rates complex is one way: SHY/TLT at 2.25, JNK/TLT at 2.16, AGG/TLT at 2.15, MBB/TLT at 2.13, and EMB/TLT at 1.90 all argue that anything with a spread to Treasuries is being bought aggressively. The TLT/IEF ratio at -2.11 confirms the pain is concentrated in the long end.

These are not mean reversion signals; they are momentum signals confirming a regime change. The one cross-asset read that might be getting stretched enough to consider fading is SPY/TLT at 2.05 and SPY/IEF at 1.87, but the underlying rate move is so powerful that even here, you wait for the z-score to roll before stepping in.
